sentences.text: The appellants/claimants are the family members of the deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- to the petitioners/appellants namely dependents of the deceased Anbalagan, who died in a motor-accident occurred on 10.07.2022.

The learned Tribunal after hearing both sides and upon considering the oral and documentary evidence has granted compensation Rs.10,65,000/- in the following manner:-
Sl . No Description

 2. Loss of love and affectio  (20,000x4)
3 . Funeral Expenses   Total

4. The Tribunal directed the above compensation to be paid by the respondents with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.
5.
The appellants/claimants, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,, have filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the accident was happened in the year 2022 at that time, the deceased was lorry technician and he earning monthly income of Rs.25,000/- but the Tribunal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 23/06/2025 11:25:43 am ) has not considering the monthly income and fixed only Rs.10,000/- is erroneous one.
He further submitted that the award passed by the Tribunal under all the heads is lower, which requires interference by this Court and prays to allow this appeal.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company submitted that there was no proof attached to show the income of the deceased.
He further submitted that the Tribunal taking into consideration all the relevant documents has rightly fixed the compensation, which does not require any interference.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of this appeal.

8. In the instant case, the deceased was lorry technician and the accident was happened in the year 2022 and considering the cost of living, this Court is enhanced the amount with regard to loss of income with future prospects (16,000+40%x12x16x1/3= Rs.14,33,600/-, for love and affection at Rs.1,76,000/-
In other aspects, the amount awarded by the Tribunal appears to be reasonable.

Therefore, the Compensation https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 23/06/2025 11:25:43 am ) award by the Tribunal is reworked as tabulated below:-
 Sl.
Description

Amount   No awarded by   Tribunal   
 
 1. For loss of income Rs.9,60,000/- R  2. Loss of love and affection Rs.80,000/- R  3. Funeral Expenses Rs.25,000/- R

In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed in part and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.10,65,000/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.16,34,600/- together with interest @ 7.5%
per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally to deposit the entire award amount now determined by this Court along with interest, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment, to the credit of MCOP.No.950 of 2022 on the file of the Special District Judge, MCOP Tribunal, Salem
